title: Refactor: Change StateDB to class based architecture.
body:
## :bookmark_tabs: Summary

- Refactors the existing stateDb implementation from a functional approach to a class-based architecture to improve code organization, maintainability, and extensibility.
- Return a new DB object when `diagramObject.db` is called.
- Introduces new StateDB class to encapsulate database operations and state
- Migrates existing functions to class methods
- Maintains existing API interface for backwards compatibility
- Following functions still uses common DB:
  - getConfig
  - getAccTitle
  - setAccTitle
  - getAccDescription
  - setAccDescription
  - getDiagramTitle
  - setDiagramTitle
- Reason why above functions still uses common DB: https://github.com/mermaid-js/mermaid/pull/6161#discussion_r1913261481

## :straight_ruler: Design Decisions

- The stateDb module previously relied on functions and global variables. Consequently, each call to mermaid.parse or mermaid.render resulted in changes to global variables.
- This behavior caused issues when rendering multiple diagrams using the same Mermaid API, as the database object (DB) for the diagrams would get mixed up.
- To address this, stateDb was refactored into a class-based structure. This change ensures that each diagramObject.db call creates a new instance of the database (DB), preventing conflicts between diagrams.

comments.author: aloisklink
comments.body: All of these constants are never changed, so we might as well just leave them outside of the `export class StateDB`, like how they were previously.
comments.label_reasoning: Constants that never change should not be instance properties of a class; they belong outside the class or as static members.

review_threads.actionability_reasoning: Suggests moving constants outside of the class, implying a concrete structural change.

comments.author: aloisklink
comments.body: This function doesn't use `this` and it's private, so we might as well just leave it how it was outside of the `export class StateDB`.
comments.label_reasoning: A private function that doesn't use 'this' has been unnecessarily moved into the class, violating good class design principles.

review_threads.actionability_reasoning: Suggests moving a private function outside of the class since it doesn't use `this`.

comments.author: aloisklink
comments.body:
This function doesn't use `this` and it's private, so we might as well just leave it outside of the `export class StateDB`.

If you want to make this PR easier to review/fix merge conflicts in, maybe you can move the function to the top of the file in a separate commit? Or, we could make this function a `static` function instead.
comments.label_reasoning: Same as index 1 — a private function not using 'this' was unnecessarily placed inside the class; should remain outside or be made static.

review_threads.actionability_reasoning: Suggests moving the function outside the class or making it `static`, with specific alternative approaches offered.

comments.author: aloisklink
comments.body:
**issue(blocking)**: This never changes!

But by making it an instance property, when you want to use `relationType`, you're doing:

https://github.com/mermaid-js/mermaid/blob/ef9bb53e670f52dd204be53e7632a8f1e84ef213/packages/mermaid/src/diagrams/state/shapes.js#L415

and then this calls `this.clear();` which is not good!

Maybe we can make it `static relationType`, so then to use it, you only need to do `StateDB.relationType.XXXXX`?
comments.label_reasoning: Making 'relationType' an instance property causes unintended side effects (triggering 'this.clear()') when accessed, which does not match the intended behavior. It should be static.

review_threads.actionability_reasoning: Flags a blocking bug where accessing an instance property triggers `this.clear()` unexpectedly, and suggests making it `static`.
